// Fixture for tests/unit/w558-test-waiters.unit.test.ts. Not compiled, not run:
// it holds the shapes the guard must NOT refuse, so that tightening the scanner
// cannot quietly start rejecting legitimate test code.

import { settle, waitUntil } from "../shared/deadline-wait.ts";

// A child process script. It contains a loop, a timer and a wall-clock read,
// but it is a string: the guard must see through the template literal.
const CHILD_SCRIPT = `
  const deadline = Date.now() + 1_000;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 5);
  }
  const retry = () => setTimeout(retry, 1);
  retry();
`;

export function childScript(): string {
  return CHILD_SCRIPT;
}

// Walking a collection is not waiting, even when it mints wall-clock values:
// expiry stamps are civil time and stay on Date.
export function expiries(offsetsMs: readonly number[]): string[] {
  const stamps: string[] = [];
  for (const offsetMs of offsetsMs) {
    stamps.push(new Date(Date.now() + offsetMs).toISOString());
  }
  return stamps;
}

// A comment mentioning a deadline loop, `while (Date.now() < deadline)`, and a
// setTimeout, must not trip the scanner. Nor must a regex like /setTimeout\(/u
// or the string "while (Date.now() < deadline) { setTimeout(f, 1); }".
export async function waits(
  ready: () => boolean,
  expect: (value: unknown) => { toBe: (other: unknown) => void },
): Promise<void> {
  await waitUntil(ready, 5_000, "Fixture readiness");
  await settle(25, "prove no further callback arrives");
  expect(ready()).toBe(true);
}
